previous_versions.body:
Useful comment from @ossie-git https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/750#issuecomment-650817817

> Before releasing any updates, I think that it should be clearly highlighted and even documented within the standard:
> 
> what types of changes are allowed in a PATCH change
> what types of changes are allowed in a MINOR change
> what types of changes are allowed in a MAJOR change

Now that 4.0.2 has been released, I think we are now in a position to discuss how we address this.

During a leaders discussion, we noted a couple of possible approaches for the next significant revision which would potentially comply with semantic versioning. We are also open to other suggestions. This new revision would come out mid-2021 at the earliest.

1) Make the next version 4.1.

In this case, we would add new requirements to the end of existing suggestions we would not remove or significantly change the meaning of existing requirements but if necessary we would retire certain requirements and add new ones. This would avoid breaking existing requirements but also provide additional or improved requirements making it easier for existing 4.0.x users. It would also potentially be a faster release.

2) Make the next version 5.0

This would be like the change from 3.x to 4.x where we make very significant changes, move requirements, remove requirments, change numbering etc. The end result would be cleaner but it would be harder to migrate.

There would be no 4.x versions released and 5.0 would probably not be released until 2022 at the earliest.



Please let us know your thoughts below.
